item.title: Entrepreneurship and Institutions in Latin America: Strategic Management of High-Impact Ventures and Entrepreneurial Ecosystems
item.content:encoded:
Veneta Andonova, Universidad de los Andes

Sascha Fuerst, Tecnologico de Monterrey

Carlos Rodriguez, INCAE Business School

Jana Schmutzler, Universidad del Norte

This special issue examines how institutional structures shape high-impact ventures in Latin American entrepreneurial ecosystems. It seeks evidence of how ventures operating under institutional voids and volatility generate effects that reshape their surrounding ecosystems, including comparative analyses of entrepreneurial output, scaling strategies, and frameworks for evaluating institutional interventions.

The special issue addresses a research gap by adopting an ecosystem-level institutional perspective on entrepreneurship in Latin America, where rapid digital adoption coexists with persistent inequality and informality. Recent disruptions from pandemics, supply-chain issues, and climate events have exposed ecosystem fragility, while policymakers experiment with regulatory sandboxes and targeted industrial policies. Contributions will inform sustainable development goals related to economic growth, innovation, and regional development.

Appel publié par European Business Review. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Institutional architectures and high-impact ventures in Latin America
  • Scaling strategies under institutional voids and resource constraints
  • Comparative metrics for entrepreneurship in the Global South
  • Entrepreneurial ecosystem intermediaries in Latin America
  • Public policy and regulatory experimentation
  • Feedback effects between firm-level choices and institutional change
